item.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
item.abstract: As AI assistants evolve into more capable agents that can access our files, emails, calendar, browser, and more, the amount of trust we’re expected to place in AI companies is growing. One startup called Maple , co-founded by a former Apple engineer who worked on privacy-preserving technologies, is taking a different approach with its AI app, where users’ data remains private — even from the company itself. “We wanted to build something that was not only encrypted but also could be proven, and that people could go look at the open-source code, and then they could look at what we call trusted execution environments,” explains Maple co-founder and CEO Mark Suman . “They can look at and verify the code that’s running on our servers, so they don’t really have to take our word for it.” “They can audit everything themselves and know how their data is being handled,” he adds. The idea of trust is Maple’s larger theme, as the startup proposes that there’s a way to build an AI app where consumers don’t have to trade privacy for convenience, as its competitors often require with their invasive privacy policies , data collection practices , and sometimes even training on users’ personal data . Instead of asking users to trust that Maple won’t misuse their personal data, it’s attempting to build a business where it can’t access that data in the first place. Image Credits: Maple.ai Like other AI apps on the market, Maple allows users to engage in a chat experience where they ask questions and get answers. Meanwhile, its newly launched desktop app, Maple Work , offers a more agentic experience where the AI can control your computer, work with your files and apps, and control your browser to get online tasks handled. With the company’s recently closed $5.3 million round, it’s moving on to its next product — a cloud-based agent that will be able to continue its work even if your computer isn’t on. This addition would make Maple more competitive with other popular consumer AI services, like Meta’s Muse , Instinct , and other AI agents that work over chat. The oversubscribed seed round was led by EPIC Ventures, with participation from Draper Associates, Planetary VC, and Epoch VC, and follows a pre-seed angel round of under a million. Maple plans to raise a Series A in the first half of 2027, given the investor interest. Screenshot Image Credits: Maple.ai Suman, who previously spent six years at Apple, already had a background where AI and privacy overlapped, he tells TechCrunch. At Apple, he worked on AI and machine learning with a particular focus on computer vision. Given Apple’s stance on consumer privacy, the challenge he faced was building products that would protect people’s identity while benefiting from computer vision techniques. His co-founder, Anthony Ronning (CTO), has a background in defense tech, security, and networking. Ronning started the company that later became Maple AI back in 2023, initially as a privacy-focused fintech. When Suman teamed up with Ronning in August 2024, the idea to create Maple AI was born. The following January, the product became available to the public as a mobile app. Image Credits: Maple.ai The app offers a familiar interface for those used to AI chatbots, but under the hood it runs a variety of open models, including versions of DeepSeek , Kimi , GLM , Inkling from Thinking Machines, Google’s Gemma , and OpenAI’s GPT OSS . Users can pick and choose the models they want or, for a simpler experience, just toggle between a quick model and the more powerful one. The models themselves run inside a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) — meaning a server with hardware encryption on it — within a U.S.-based data center. (Maple also offers support for European customers through a partner that runs its server in Europe). “We actually don’t have access to [the data] while it’s inside the TEE,” explains Suman. “The data gets encrypted first on your device using a unique password that’s only known by you, the user — we don’t have access to it. It then goes into this TEE, and it gets decrypted inside there. The AI does its thing, and then it re-encrypts it with your password and sends it back to you,” he continues. “So we provide an end-to-end experience that’s very easy for the user, but we actually don’t have access to the raw data as it’s in flight or even when it’s at rest,” he adds. This allows Maple to protect its users’ data, even from outsiders — like if hackers breached its system or the government came with a subpoena, for instance. All it could do would be to hand over an encrypted file. “We just simply don’t want access to it,” Suman says of customers’ data. “That’s not part of our business model. And we also don’t want it to be part of our threat model.” Image Credits: Maple.ai With the new desktop app, Maple is looking to small businesses who may want to benefit from AI without the data privacy risks. Inside the app, there’s an integration store where users can connect with other apps, like their Gmail or calendar. The desktop app can also spin up a subagent that works inside another AI app you may have on your desktop, like Claude, Codex, or others that support the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). This allows customers to use their preferred AI app for specific tasks, without having to give it all their information — just what’s needed for the given task. Next year, Maple plans to enter the enterprise market with pilot work, where it will offer its own version of zero data retention. (Maple doesn’t retain most of the customers’ data, but when it has to, that data is encrypted.) It’s now in the process of completing SOC 2 compliance and security audits to get ready for this expansion. The company declined to share its registered customer numbers, but noted it’s seen 60x growth over the past three months, as people have been looking for ways to increase their security with AI. Maple currently generates revenue via subscriptions, which are comparable to those from other AI model providers. Its Pro plan is $20 per month, and it offers two Max plans, Max and Max Plus, at $100 and $200 per month, respectively. The Austin- and San Francisco-based startup is a team of four and is actively hiring.

item.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
item.abstract: The U.K. government’s cybersecurity unit says it has seen a “marked rise” in AI-driven cyberattacks in recent months, as hackers increasingly rely on autonomous hacking tools to identify and exploit simple weaknesses to break into systems and networks. The U.K. National Cybersecurity Center (NCSC) said it has seen several cyber incidents since September involving autonomous hacking tools, such as penetration testing tools used by defenders to stress-test their cybersecurity defenses. These incidents have caused intrusions at organizations and resulted in downtime, the unit said in a blog post . The NCSC says that while none of the vulnerabilities being exploited are new, the speed at which these AI tools are able to carry out simple hacks has changed. The rise in AI-related cyberattacks coincides with the broader release earlier this year of open source autonomous penetration testing tools like Artex and Cairn, among others, which anyone can download and use at no cost. The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation recently warned that malicious hackers are using AI penetration testing tools to carry out cyberattacks at unprecedented speeds. While cyberattacks and intrusions are on the rise, the message from London is that many of these attacks are preventable with basic cybersecurity defenses and best practices. “Notably, the issues being exploited currently are not novel memory corruption vulnerabilities (or even known but unpatched vulnerabilities), but unmitigated weaknesses that are often the result of years of technical debt that organisations have accumulated,” the NCSC wrote. The unit said that agentic hacking tools often look for exposed or internet-facing systems, then quickly run through lists of weak or easy-to-guess passwords or abuse API endpoints often used by developers to access data. The NCSC said that AI “does not make established cyber security controls obsolete,” but rather that “building strong foundations has never mattered more.” The unit added that AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities and faster to exploit them, warning that weaknesses that have gone unnoticed for years can now be found in minutes.

item.title: 7 Most Downloaded AI Models on Hugging Face
item.abstract: 7 Most Downloaded AI Models on Hugging Face The most downloaded AI models on Hugging Face aren't the ones you'd expect. Discover why smaller, older, and specialized models dominate the rankings. By Abid Ali Awan , KDnuggets Assistant Editor on November 24, 2026 in Artificial Intelligence You might expect models like Llama , Qwen , DeepSeek , or Mistral to dominate the most-downloaded AI models on Hugging Face . Surprisingly, the list looks very different. Instead of massive language models, we see small embedding models, rerankers, speech recognition systems, and even older models like GPT-2 and BERT. Why? Because downloads don't necessarily reflect which models are the most powerful or popular among AI enthusiasts. They often reflect how frequently models are used in applications, research experiments, automated workflows, and tutorials. Let's explore seven of the most downloaded models on Hugging Face, what they do, and why they remain so popular. 1. all-MiniLM-L6-v2 This lightweight sentence embedding model converts text into 384-dimensional vectors that represent its meaning. It's widely used for semantic search, document similarity, clustering, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Its popularity comes from its simplicity, small size, and efficiency. You can run it on a CPU, integrate it into Python applications, and build useful search systems without needing an expensive GPU. It's also one of the most commonly used models in beginner tutorials, making it a natural choice for developers experimenting with embeddings. Downloads: 182,461,837 2. ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 This cross-encoder model specializes in reranking search results. For example, a search engine might retrieve 20 relevant documents using embeddings. This model then compares each document with the original query and assigns a relevance score to improve the ranking. It's especially useful in RAG pipelines, enterprise search, and question-answering applications. Although it doesn't generate answers like ChatGPT , it helps applications retrieve better information before passing it to a language model. Downloads: 66,397,898 3. bge-small-en-v1.5 Developed by the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI), bge-small-en-v1.5 is a feature extraction model that converts text into 384-dimensional embeddings. These embeddings capture semantic meaning, making the model useful for semantic search, document retrieval, text similarity, and RAG applications. Its popularity comes from its small size, fast inference, and ability to run locally without requiring expensive hardware. It's also widely integrated into vector databases, retrieval frameworks, and AI tutorials. Downloads: 49,421,693 4. MiniMax-H3 Unlike the previous models, MiniMax-H3 focuses on video generation. This particular repository contains model files repackaged for ComfyUI , a popular node-based interface for generative AI workflows. Developers and creators can use these models for text-to-video, image-to-video, and other video-generation workflows. Its presence shows that Hugging Face is not just about language models. Creative AI tools and their supporting model files can also generate significant download activity. Downloads: 31,821,266 5. GPT-2 GPT-2 , released by OpenAI in 2019, might seem outdated compared with today's language models. However, it remains useful for learning, research, benchmarking, and experimenting with text generation. Its relatively small size makes it practical for Google Colab notebooks, educational projects, and experiments involving fine-tuning or language model internals. Many tutorials and research implementations still reference GPT-2, contributing to its continued download activity. Downloads: 29,775,719 6. bert-base-uncased Introduced by Google in 2018, BERT helped transform natural language processing (NLP). Unlike modern chat-oriented generative models, BERT is an encoder model designed to understand and represent text. It's commonly fine-tuned for text classification, named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, and other NLP tasks. BERT remains a standard baseline in research and education, and many applications continue to use its architecture. Downloads: 29,590,515 7. Chronos-2 Chronos-2 is a 120-million-parameter time series forecasting model designed to predict future values from historical data. Unlike traditional language models, it specializes in forecasting patterns in data such as stock prices, electricity demand, retail sales, and weather measurements. It supports univariate and multivariate forecasting, meaning it can predict a single variable or multiple related variables. It can also incorporate additional information, such as holidays or other known future events, to improve its predictions. Its popularity comes from its small size, fast inference, and ability to generate forecasts without task-specific training. Developers can run it locally on CPUs or GPUs, making it useful for research, forecasting experiments, and practical business applications. Downloads: 24,324,549 Why Aren't the Biggest Large Language Models at the Top? There are several reasons why these smaller and older models receive so many downloads. Automatic downloads: When someone runs a tutorial, Google Colab notebook, or application using a Hugging Face model, the required files can be downloaded automatically. Repeated runs across environments can contribute to download counts. Research and education: Models like BERT and GPT-2 are established research baselines. Thousands of tutorials, experiments, and academic projects continue to use them. item.title: Q&A: How Everstone Brings Where Winds Meet to Life with NVIDIA DLSS 5
item.abstract: Where Winds Meet moves between distant mountain landscapes, bustling streets, and quiet moments with its characters. For Everstone Studio, bringing more realistic lighting and materials to this wuxia world means keeping its aesthetics, recognizable characters, and carefully composed atmosphere intact. The team’s ongoing work with NVIDIA DLSS and Streamline provided a foundation for integrating DLSS 5. Artists and engineers evaluated its lighting and material enhancements against the game’s art direction, balancing visual gains with additional performance overhead. We sat down with art director Muzi Li and engine tech lead Cory Zhou to discuss the studio’s integration approach, preserving character identity, the changes that stood out in Jiangnan, and why developers should account for DLSS 5 early in their rendering budgets. Video 1. Where Winds Meet with DLSS 5 What made DLSS 5 a fit for Where Winds Meet ? The world of Where Winds Meet encompasses landscapes and towns, as well as countless details in how people interact with their surroundings. Players might be gazing into the distance from a mountain one moment, then walking down a bustling street the next. We want these scenes to be more than beautiful; we want players to feel their different weather conditions, times of day, and moods. What attracts us to DLSS 5 is the room it gives us to explore lighting and materials further. It builds on the image already produced by the game engine, using neural rendering to enhance lighting and material details. Our goal isn’t to pursue greater visual impact for its own sake. It’s to make these details work in harmony with the original art direction: distant landscapes should retain their poetic atmosphere, while nearby buildings and characters should have a believable sense of texture. What were your art team’s first thoughts of DLSS 5? Our first impression was that the interplay of light and shadow had gained greater depth. When sunlight falls on buildings, fabrics, and characters, the result feels more than just a sharper image. DLSS 5 identifies and tones down overly bright highlights while bringing out more detail in those areas. It also fills in ambient-light details and subtle highlights in the shadows, and recognizes the properties of materials. How did you integrate DLSS 5 into your pipeline? We have consistently integrated the latest DLSS technologies and kept our NVIDIA Streamline integration up to date. As a result, our rendering pipeline already had strong support for DLSS, providing a solid foundation for adopting DLSS 5. This ongoing investment made the upgrade a natural extension of our existing technology roadmap and helped ensure a smooth integration process. How did artists and engineers use DLSS 5 controls to preserve art direction across characters, materials, and lighting? In any given scene, we look at whether characters remain recognizable, whether materials such as fabric, leather, and metal are still visually distinct, and whether changes in lighting and shadow disrupt the scene’s original mood. NVIDIA provides developers with options for model selection and controls over aspects such as structural and tonal strength. For us, artists and engineers need to communicate and iterate based on what we see on screen. One setting might make the environment more striking, but if faces or the overall color palette drift away from the intended look, we need to find a different balance. We want to strike the right balance between visual gains, performance cost, and player preferences, while giving players choices wherever possible. How did you evaluate DLSS 5 image quality and performance? Our evaluation focuses on three key areas: visual quality, performance overhead, and alignment with the game’s artistic direction. Our testing to date indicates that enabling DLSS 5 introduces additional performance overhead, so we assess that cost alongside the visual improvements it delivers. In developing Where Winds Meet , we have consistently explored different graphics technologies to support a wide range of player preferences. In our internal playtesting, DLSS 5 delivered a distinct visual experience, enhancing the overall presentation of our environments and their sense of immersion. Based on these findings, we plan to give players the option to enable or disable DLSS 5. Our approach to visual tuning will be guided by the art team’s creative vision, including selecting the DLSS 5 model that best matches the intended aesthetic. We also aim to make relevant visual controls available to players wherever possible, allowing them to tailor the image to their preferences. On balance, our evaluation has been positive, taking into account the visual improvements, performance overhead, and flexibility offered to players. How does DLSS 5 affect characters? What matters is whether characters feel more naturally part of the world while retaining their own distinctive presence. For example, when a character walks from sunlight into the shade beneath an eave, changes in lighting and materials can help them feel more naturally grounded in the environment. The way different clothing materials respond to light can also give them a stronger presence. At the same time, we pay close attention to whether faces and costumes remain recognizable. Which scene best demonstrates the improvements? We find that Jiangnan is where DLSS 5 makes the biggest visual improvement. \When adjusting the settings, we use DLSS 5 to soften highlights in the original scene lighting that can appear too harsh, while adding a greater sense of depth between buildings. DLSS 5 can recognize ambient color from the sun and fill in details in darker areas, giving shadows more depth and material detail. Many buildings in Jiangnan feature wood and tiled roofs; DLSS 5 can fill in lifelike wood and roof-tile details. As for the image that best showcases the effect, it will reveal itself during each player’s own journey: perhaps at a street corner just after the rain has cleared, or at an old ferry crossing bathed in the setting sun—a quiet moment that makes you stop and linger. What advice would you give other developers adopting DLSS 5? First, account for DLSS 5 performance requirements early in your rendering budget. For projects targeting high frame rates, reserve sufficient performance headroom and evaluate the balance between visual benefits and performance cost in representative gameplay scenarios. Second, work closely with the NVIDIA team throughout integration and tuning to understand the technology’s capabilities and available controls. Align that work with your project’s artistic direction and performance targets. item.title: Tidal bans AI-generated music
item.abstract:
Nov 24, 2026 7:06am PT Tidal Bans AI-Generated Music Tidal The music streaming service Tidal said Tuesday that it would ban tracks it believes are completely AI-generated starting next month, a move its leader believes “will resonate with both artists and listeners alike.” The service will remove the AI tracks starting Dec. 9, making Tidal the first music streaming platform to ban AI music entirely. It comes nearly five months after Tidal said it would demonetize any AI-powered song, force those artists to label their tracks as either AI-generated or AI-assisted and ban AI songs that were associated with “fraudulent activity,” a category that includes songs impersonating established artists and efforts to “deceive listeners.” “But that’s enough, as 43% of tracks distributed to us in the last 90 days have been detected as AI-generated. Something more drastic needs to be done,” wrote Robert Andersen, the Tidal Lead at parent company Block, in an X thread on Tuesday. “We’ll begin removing all wholly AI-generated tracks from our catalog, and you’ll see them completely gone by the beginning of the year.” Andersen said that 96% of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays. The move will cleave the platform of 29 million tracks, he added, and have it reject between 80,000 to 85,000 songs a day. “We encourage our peers to follow suit,” he wrote. The move comes as competitors such as Spotify and Apple Music continue to test approaches to combat the rise of AI-generated tracks proliferating on their platforms, many of which the services have labeled some version of “slop” or “spam.” Apple Music said it would also begin labeling AI-generated or AI-assisted tracks on its platform, while Spotify said it would label artists it deemed AI creations as an “AI Persona.” Spotify said in a blog post last month it also removed 50 million slop or spam tracks from users’ recommendations this year, which came after it removed 75 million of those songs from its catalog entirely. The revelation came among a number of updates regarding Spotify’s efforts to combat AI spam. “This work isn’t finished,” Spotify added. “AI moves fast, and bad actors adapt just as fast. But as AI makes music more abundant, we believe listeners will value human artistry even more.
